title: AWS NAT Gateway Port Allocation Exhaustion During Flash Sale
description: High outbound packet loss and 504 timeouts when payment service attempts to reach Stripe API. Latency spiked from 80ms to 15,000ms. Database CPU is under 15%.

error_logs: 2026-09-17T00:15:33Z [payment-worker] dial tcp 52.39.22.84:443: connect: connection timed out

network.title: AWS NAT Gateway SNAT Port Exhaustion Runbook
network.raw_content:
# AWS NAT Gateway SNAT Exhaustion Runbook

## Root Cause Indicators
- CloudWatch Metric: `ErrorPortAllocation` > 0
- CloudWatch Metric: `PacketsDropCount` > 0
Each NAT gateway supports a maximum of 55,000 concurrent connections per destination IP. When multiple container instances burst outbound traffic without connection pooling, source port allocation fails.

## Diagnostic Commands
```bash
aws cloudwatch get-metric-data --metric-data-queries '...' --start-time -1h
```

## Immediate Mitigation
1. Allocate a secondary elastic IP to the NAT Gateway to double the available SNAT ports (from 55,000 to 110,000).
2. Provision an additional NAT Gateway in AZ-b and balance route tables.

application.title: Payment Worker HTTP Client Pooling
application.raw_content:
# Payment Service HTTP Client Configuration

## Connection Pool Settings
Payment worker uses `http.DefaultTransport` with `MaxIdleConnsPerHost = 100`. Verify that client connections are properly reusing TCP sockets and closing response bodies.

database.title: Database Health During Outbound Outages
database.raw_content:
# Database Status Check
During third-party payment gateway outages, confirm that database is not accumulating uncommitted locks waiting on network timeouts.

security.title: Security Group and Egress Filter Verification
security.raw_content:
# Network Egress Security Verification
Ensure that security group egress rules allow TCP port 443 outbound to 0.0.0.0/0 and no AWS Network Firewall drop rules were deployed.
